The Belt Trick

A solid spins inside a cage, a belt running from each of its faces to the cage. The belts twist and wind as it turns, and never pass through one another. After one full turn the solid is back where it started and the belts are tangled. After two they have untangled themselves, and everything is back.

That is Dirac's belt trick. A rotation turned through a full turn cannot be shrunk back to doing nothing; turned through two, it can. Physicists meet it as the reason an electron must turn twice to return to its starting state.

Drag to turn the view. Space plays and pauses, the arrow keys step, and [ ] change the speed. At 1× one full cycle — two turns — takes twelve seconds.

Computed in your browser by a port of the project's Belt Trick generator, checked against it to a millionth of a millimetre. After Hanson, Visualizing Quaternions (2006), ch. 12; Pengelley and Ramras (2017); Francis and Kauffman, "Air on the Dirac strings" (1994); Holroyd's spinor linkage (2021).
